channel.title: Via blog
channel.description: We're making Via better every day! Subscribe to keep up to date with our progress.

item.title: Wyvern, a Snapdragon module on one flat board
item.description: Wyvern is a Snapdragon development board laid out like a Teensy, the small microcontroller board.

item.title: Signet, a mouse worn as a ring of flat boards
item.description: Signet is a computer mouse you wear as a ring on your index finger. Eight small circuit boards sit round the finger, each soldered to the next along its edge.

item.title: Rosetta, a controller whose knob picks the console
item.description: Rosetta is one game controller for a PS4, a PS5, an Xbox, a Switch or anything over Bluetooth. A five-position knob, where an Xbox 360 pad has its guide button, picks the console.

item.title: Lark, a voice-controlled ceiling-fan bulb on four boards
item.description: Lark is a ceiling-fan light bulb designed for voice control, with the speech recognition inside the bulb. It screws into the fan's E26 socket and runs on 120 V mains.

item.title: Hush, a speaker that plays the inverse of what it hears
item.description: Hush is a ring of circuit board that sits on the face of a 40 mm speaker. A microphone on its hub hears the noise in front of the cone, and the speaker plays its opposite.

item.title: Basalt: fitting a Threadripper onto a microATX board
item.description: Basalt is a motherboard for AMD's Threadripper 7000 and 9000 processors, on a microATX board 244 mm square.

item.title: Herald: answering a fire panel's phone call in firmware
item.description: Herald is a board designed to sit beside a fire alarm panel and pass on its reports. Many panels report by dialing a monitoring station on a phone line, and Herald stands in for that line.
